newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BREWER DOJLIDY TO INVEST PLN 100 MLN.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BREWER DOJLIDY TO INVEST PLN 100 MLN.

text.p: Polish brewer Dojlidy Sp. z o.o. plans to invest 100 million zlotys in the next three years to increase its 2.1-percent market share after Poland's expected entry to the European Union, the firm's trade director said.
Dojlidy is 49-percent owned by German brewer Binding Brauerei AG and 48-percent owned by Polish investment firm Ambresa SA, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA (BRE) .
"From our resources and through the company's capital increase we want to invest 100 million zlotys in the course of three years," Jolanta Czemiel told a Thursday news conference.
Czemiel said Dojlidy, based in the northern city of Bialystok, had a 1.7-percent market share in 1996.
But she said that in northeast Poland the firm was dominant with a share of over 50 percent.
Dojlidy plans to produce 450,000 hectolitres of beer this year and one million hectolitres annually in three years.
"Everyone should be prepared in terms of production and packaging for EU entry," Czemiel said.
